title: Spelt and honey rolls
subtitle: soft, slightly sweet yeasted dinner rolls made with spelt flour
excerpt: Spelt and honey rolls are soft, slightly sweet yeasted dinner rolls made with a blend of spelt and strong white flour. The spelt gives a mild, slightly nutty flavour and a tender crumb. Honey adds a quiet sweetness without making the rolls taste sugary. The dough is enriched with butter and egg, which keeps the rolls soft and pillowy through the day. They bake in about 20 minutes.
sourceNotes: Spelt flour in breadmaking is documented across Europe from antiquity. Enriched dinner rolls with honey or sugar are documented in British and American baking from the nineteenth century onward.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked rolls in an airtight bag for up to 2 months. Reheat from frozen in a hot oven for 8 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape the rolls and refrigerate overnight for a slow second proof. Remove from the fridge an hour before baking to come to room temperature.

content.text: Spelt and honey rolls are enriched dinner rolls made with a blend of white spelt and strong white flour. The spelt gives a slightly earthy, nutty flavour; the honey and butter make the crumb soft and tender. The dough rises predictably and handles well. The rolls bake quickly and are best eaten the same day, though they reheat well.

Combine both flours, instant yeast, and salt in a large bowl. Add the honey, softened butter, egg, and warm milk. Mix together until a shaggy dough forms, then knead for 8 minutes until smooth, soft, and slightly tacky. The dough is enriched and will feel softer than a plain bread dough.
Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for about 60 minutes until doubled.

Turn the dough out and divide into 12 equal pieces (about 60 g each). Roll each piece under a cupped palm on an unfloured surface into a smooth, taut ball. Place on a lined baking tray, close together so they touch as they prove.
Cover loosely with oiled cling film and leave to prove for 40 to 45 minutes until puffed and just touching their neighbours.

Heat the oven to 200 degrees C (fan 180 degrees C / gas 6). Brush the rolls with beaten egg. Bake for 18 to 22 minutes until deep golden on top. Leave to cool on the tray for 5 minutes; they will tear apart along the joined edges.

attrs.avoid: Avoid adding the salt directly onto the yeast before mixing; salt inhibits yeast activity.
attrs.fix: Add salt to the flour first and mix through before adding the wet ingredients including the yeast. If the dough has risen slowly, extend the bulk fermentation until the dough is clearly doubled before dividing.

attrs.problem: Rolls dry and tough the same day
attrs.avoid: Avoid overbaking and avoid leaving the rolls uncovered while cooling; they dry out quickly once the crust is pierced.
attrs.fix: Remove when the tops are golden and the internal temperature is around 90 degrees C. Wrap in a tea towel for the first 10 minutes of cooling to soften the crust.
